findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-arg version
findings.body: `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the second definition wins, so any existing caller passing width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)`) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4), and `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` would be interpreted as dimensions=100, opts=100. Keep a single method with an unambiguous signature (e.g. accept a dimensions string only, and update all callers).

findings.title: Downsize loop can spin without progress and still upload an oversized image
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but ignores its return value. If the ImageMagick/gifsicle invocation fails (`convert_with` returns false), the tempfile is unchanged and the loop simply burns 5 iterations before passing an image that still exceeds `max_image_size_kb` to `Upload.create_for`. Likewise, 5 × 80% reductions may not be enough for a very large upload, so an oversized image is still accepted. Check the return value, break on failure, and handle the still-too-large case explicitly (error to the user).

findings.title: Animated GIF detection fails because tempfile paths have no .gif extension
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which for uploaded files is a generic Tempfile path with no image extension, so animated GIFs are processed with `convert #{from}[0]`, which keeps only the first frame and destroys the animation of the user's upload. Pass the original filename/extension or create the tempfile with the proper extension.

findings.title: Client-side max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Sites configured with a lower (or higher) `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` will have client validation disagree with the server: attachments larger than the configured limit pass client validation and then fail server-side, and the error message shows the wrong limit. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler (line 246) reports a misleading size to users.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap. Sites that intentionally restrict upload size can now have up to 10MB fetched from arbitrary API-supplied URLs regardless of their setting, increasing disk/bandwidth exposure. Derive the cap from a setting instead.
